newsitem.title: THAILAND: Trading resumes in Bkk Bank of Commerce.
newsitem.headline: Trading resumes in Bkk Bank of Commerce.

text.p: Troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc fell 12.00 baht to 4.00 baht on the Stock Exchange of Thailand shortly after its 11-month suspension was lifted on Thursday.

The Thai bourse said last Friday it would allow the bank, taken over by the government last May for incurring massive loan losses, to resume trading for one month before deciding whether it should be delisted.
The stock fell further to 3.6 baht six minutes after opening but later recovered to 4.1 baht.
The bank told the bourse last week that it faced a huge 24.85 billion baht ($955 million) net loss in 1996 against a 860.4 million baht profit in 1995.
The stock exchange said the bank's outstanding tangible assets amounting to less than 50 percent of its 35.5 billion baht paid-up capital made it a candidate for delisting.
The bourse said it would give Bangkok Bank of Commerce's shareholders and investors a chance to trade its shares between April 17 and May 16. From May 19, the stock would be suspended again.
The bank said last week its net non-performing loans, after collateral deduction, rose to 53.78 billion baht at end-1996 from 36.58 billion a year earlier.
Its outstanding loans and interest receivables stood at 87.1 billion baht last December against 64.4 billion a year ago.

The central bank has assigned industrial financing bank Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand Plc to manage the bank for seven years in exchange for an option to buy a future majority equity stake in the ailing bank.
